exercises.name: Squat Reach
exercises.overview: A dynamic squat variation that adds an overhead reach to increase mobility and coordination.
exercises.benefits: Improves lower body mobility activates legs and warms up hips and shoulders
exercises.instructions:
Keep feet shoulder-width apart and chest upright throughout.
Push hips back and bend knees to lower into the squat.
As you stand, extend hips fully and reach both arms overhead.

exercises.name: Jumping Squats
exercises.overview: A plyometric squat designed to develop explosive leg power.
exercises.benefits: Increases leg power boosts cardiovascular intensity and improves athletic performance
exercises.instructions:
Start with feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a controlled squat.
Drive through your heels and jump explosively upward.
Land softly with bent knees and flow straight into the next squat.

exercises.name: Squat Kicks
exercises.overview: A dynamic lower body movement combining squats and alternating kicks.
exercises.benefits: Improves coordination balance and lower body endurance
exercises.instructions:
Lower into a squat with feet shoulder-width apart and core tight.
As you rise, extend one leg forward in a controlled kick.
Return the foot down and alternate legs with each rep.

exercises.name: Burpee Jump
exercises.overview: A high intensity full body conditioning movement combining squat plank and jump.
exercises.benefits: Raises heart rate quickly improves endurance and full body strength
exercises.instructions:
Drop into a squat, place hands on the floor, and kick feet back to plank.
Return feet to hands quickly and keep your core tight throughout.
Jump explosively upward and reach arms overhead to complete the rep.

exercises.name: Push Ups
exercises.overview: A classic upper body strength exercise using bodyweight resistance.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens chest shoulders triceps and core stability
exercises.instructions:
Keep hands slightly wider than shoulders and body in a straight line.
Lower chest toward the floor with elbows bending in a controlled manner.
Push through palms to return to start without letting hips sag.

exercises.name: T Plank
exercises.overview: A plank variation that introduces rotation and shoulder stability work.
exercises.benefits: Enhances core stability shoulder control and balance
exercises.instructions:
Start in a solid plank with hands under shoulders and body aligned.
Rotate torso to one side and lift one arm toward the ceiling.
Hold briefly, return to plank, and alternate sides with control.

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.overview: A foundational lower body exercise focused on unilateral leg strength.
exercises.benefits: Builds leg strength improves balance and enhances mobility
exercises.instructions:
Step forward and lower hips until both knees are at right angles.
Keep torso upright and front knee aligned over the foot.
Push through the front heel to return to standing then alternate legs.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.overview: A fast paced core and cardio exercise performed from a plank position.
exercises.benefits: Improves cardiovascular fitness core strength and agility
exercises.instructions:
Hold a strong high plank with hands directly under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward the chest while the other leg stays extended.
Switch legs quickly in a running motion without letting hips rise.

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.overview: A classic aerobic exercise often used during warm ups.
exercises.benefits: Increases heart rate improves coordination and warms the entire body
exercises.instructions:
Start with feet together and arms by your sides.
Jump feet outward while raising arms overhead in a wide arc.
Jump back to start and keep a steady rhythmic pace throughout.

exercises.name: Walking Hip Opener
exercises.overview: A dynamic warm-up exercise where the hip is lifted and externally rotated while walking to improve mobility.
exercises.benefits: Increases hip mobility activates glutes and prepares lower body for movement
exercises.instructions:
Step forward and lift the knee toward the chest as you walk.
Rotate the lifted leg outward to open the hip with torso tall.
Place the foot down and repeat the same movement with the opposite leg.

exercises.name: Straight Leg March
exercises.overview: A dynamic walking exercise that stretches the hamstrings, activates core stability, and improves dynamic balance.
exercises.benefits: Stretches hamstrings dynamically and improves single-leg balance which activates core and enhances hip mobility and coordination
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall with chest up and chin up and transfer weight onto one foot. 
kick the opposite leg up as high as comfortably possible without bending it, and simultaneously extend the opposite arm to meet the foot.
Pull the leg back down, step forward, and repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Leg Raise To Knee Tuck
exercises.overview: A core exercise combining leg raises with knee tucks to maximize abdominal engagement.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower abs improves control and enhances core coordination
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with legs extended and arms by your sides.
Lift legs then bend knees toward chest while raising hips slightly.
Extend legs back out and lower down in control.

exercises.name: Split Jump
exercises.overview: A plyometric lower body exercise where the athlete jumps from a split lunge and switches legs midair.
exercises.benefits: Develops explosive leg power improves coordination and increases cardiovascular intensity
exercises.instructions:
Begin in a lunge with torso upright and core engaged.
Jump explosively and switch leg positions in midair.
Land softly in the opposite lunge with bent knees and immediately reset.

exercises.name: Press Up Position Toe Tap
exercises.overview: A plank variation where one foot taps outward to challenge stability and core control.
exercises.benefits: Improves core stability enhances shoulder endurance and develops coordination
exercises.instructions:
Start in a high plank with hands directly under shoulders.
Lift one foot and tap it out to the side keeping hips stable.
Return foot to start and alternate sides while maintaining plank form.

exercises.name: Abdominal Crunches
exercises.overview: A classic core exercise performed on the floor where the upper body curls toward the knees, isolating the abdominal muscles without lifting the lower back off the ground.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens and tones abdominal muscles; improves core stability and posture; trims waistline; enhances balance and stability
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, hands on chest or behind head.
Contract your abs and lift your shoulders off the floor, curling toward your knees.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.overview: A plyometric lower body exercise where the athlete jumps from the ground onto an elevated surface.
exercises.benefits: Develops explosive leg power improves coordination and enhances lower body strength
exercises.instructions:
Stand facing the box with feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend knees, swing arms back, and jump explosively onto the platform.
Land softly with bent knees then step down carefully before repeating.

exercises.name: Cobra Stretch
exercises.overview: A floor based spinal extension stretch commonly used in yoga and mobility routines.
exercises.benefits: Improves spinal mobility stretches abdominal muscles and helps reduce stiffness from prolonged sitting
exercises.instructions:
Lie face down with legs extended and palms placed under shoulders.
Press through hands to lift the chest while keeping hips on the floor.
Hold the stretch briefly then lower torso back down with control.

exercises.name: Punches
exercises.overview: A simple cardio exercise inspired by boxing movements performed without equipment.
exercises.benefits: Increases cardiovascular activity improves coordination and strengthens shoulders and arms
exercises.instructions:
Keep knees slightly bent, core engaged, and stance stable.
Extend one arm forward with a slight torso rotation for power.
Quickly retract and alternate arms in a steady controlled rhythm.

exercises.name: Wide Arm Push Up
exercises.overview: A push-up variation where the hands are positioned wider to emphasize chest activation.
exercises.benefits: Increases chest engagement strengthens shoulders and improves upper body pushing strength
exercises.instructions:
Place hands wider than shoulders and keep body in a straight line.
Lower chest toward the floor with elbows flaring slightly outward.
Push through palms to return to start while keeping core tight.

exercises.name: Shoulder Stretch
exercises.overview: A simple upper body stretch that targets the shoulder muscles and improves joint mobility.
exercises.benefits: Improves shoulder flexibility reduces stiffness and helps prevent injury during upper body exercises
exercises.instructions:
Extend one arm straight across the chest at shoulder height.
Use the opposite hand to gently pull the arm closer to the body.
Keep the shoulder relaxed, hold briefly, then switch arms.

exercises.name: Leg Raise Hold
exercises.overview: A static core exercise where legs are held at an angle to build abdominal strength.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower abs improves endurance and enhances core stability
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with legs extended and arms by your sides.
Raise legs to about 45 degrees while keeping them straight.
Hold position then lower legs in control.

exercises.name: Seated Abs Circles
exercises.overview: A seated core stability exercise where the legs move in circular patterns to engage abdominal muscles.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens the core improves hip control and enhances abdominal endurance
exercises.instructions:
Sit with knees bent, feet lifted, and torso slightly leaned back.
Engage the core and move knees together in a circular motion.
Keep core tight throughout and reverse the direction after several reps.

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.overview: A dynamic mobility exercise that transitions from standing to plank by walking the hands forward.
exercises.benefits: Improves hamstring flexibility activates the core and warms up the shoulders and posterior chain
exercises.instructions:
Bend forward from standing and place hands flat on the floor.
Walk hands forward until body reaches a high plank with core engaged.
Walk feet toward hands with legs relatively straight then return to standing.

exercises.name: Step Up on Chair
exercises.overview: A functional lower body exercise where the body steps onto an elevated surface using leg strength.
exercises.benefits: Builds leg strength improves balance and enhances functional movement ability
exercises.instructions:
Place one foot firmly on the chair and stand upright with core engaged.
Push through the heel to lift your body until the leg is fully extended.
Step down with control and alternate legs each rep.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge hold
exercises.overview: A bodyweight exercise that strengthens the glutes and posterior chain by lifting the hips from a supine position.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens glutes and hamstrings, improves hip stability, supports lower back health, activates posterior chain.
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Press through heels and lift hips until body forms a straight line.
Squeeze glutes at the top then lower slowly and repeat with control.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
exercises.overview: A core stability exercise performed in a plank position while alternating shoulder taps to challenge balance and anti-rotation control.
exercises.benefits: Improves core stability, strengthens shoulders, enhances balance and coordination, trains anti-rotation control.
exercises.instructions:
Hold a high plank with feet slightly wider apart for stability.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder while keeping hips still.
Return hand to floor and alternate sides in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.overview: A standing cardio exercise where alternating knees are driven upward rapidly to simulate running in place.
exercises.benefits: Elevates heart rate quickly improves cardiovascular endurance strengthens hip flexors and enhances coordination
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and keep your core tight throughout.
Drive one knee up toward the chest and pump the opposite arm simultaneously.
Switch legs quickly in a running motion without letting your posture drop.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.overview: A floor-based stability exercise where opposite arm and leg are extended simultaneously to challenge core control and balance.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens core and lower back improves balance and coordination and helps prevent lower back pain
exercises.instructions:
Start on all fours with hands under shoulders, knees under hips and back flat.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping hips level and core tight.
Hold briefly, return to start and repeat on the other side with control.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunches
exercises.overview: A core focused abdominal exercise where the hips lift off the floor to target the lower abdominals.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower abdominal muscles improves core stability and supports spinal control
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet lifted off the floor.
Curl hips upward lifting knees toward the chest using core strength only.
Lower hips slowly with control and avoid using momentum.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.overview: A static core exercise that builds strength by holding a straight body position.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens core improves stability and enhances posture
exercises.instructions:
Place forearms under shoulders with legs extended behind.
Keep body straight and core engaged without dropping hips.
Hold position steadily while maintaining control.

exercises.name: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)
exercises.overview: Foundational standing yoga pose focusing on alignment, balance, and body awareness with the body upright and stable.
exercises.benefits: Improves posture, enhances balance, strengthens the legs and core, increases body awareness, and promotes relaxation.
exercises.instructions:
Stand upright with your feet together or hip-width apart and distribute your weight evenly across both feet.
Engage your thighs and core, lengthen your spine, and roll your shoulders back and down while keeping your arms relaxed at your sides.
Hold the position steady, maintain proper alignment, and breathe slowly and deeply.

exercises.name: Tree Pose (Vrikshasana)
exercises.overview: A standing balance pose where one foot is placed on the opposite leg, improving stability and concentration.
exercises.benefits: Improves balance, strengthens legs and core, enhances focus, promotes stability, and supports posture
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall and shift your weight onto one leg while keeping your balance steady.
Place the sole of your opposite foot on your inner calf or thigh and bring your hands together.
Hold steady, fix your gaze on one point, and breathe slowly.

exercises.name: Child’s Pose (Balasana)
exercises.overview: A resting yoga pose where the body folds forward, promoting relaxation and gentle stretching of the back and hips.
exercises.benefits: Relieves lower back tension, stretches hips and thighs, promotes relaxation, reduces stress, and improves flexibility
exercises.instructions:
Kneel on the floor and sit back on your heels while keeping your knees together or slightly apart.
Bend forward and rest your torso between your thighs with your arms extended or relaxed.
Rest your forehead down, relax your body, and breathe deeply.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Pose (Marjaryasana–Bitilasana)
exercises.movement_pattern: spinal flexion; spinal extension; dynamic flow
exercises.overview: A gentle flowing sequence between two poses that warms up the spine and improves mobility through coordinated breathing.
exercises.benefits: Improves spinal flexibility, relieves back tension, enhances posture, promotes mobility, and supports relaxation
exercises.instructions:
Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale as you drop your belly, lift your chest, and look slightly upward.
Exhale as you round your spine, tuck your chin, and draw your belly inward.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Bend (Paschimottanasana)
exercises.overview: A seated forward fold that stretches the entire posterior chain, especially the hamstrings and lower back, while calming the mind.
exercises.benefits: Stretches hamstrings and spine, relieves lower back tension, improves flexibility, promotes relaxation, and supports digestion
exercises.instructions:
Sit upright with your legs extended straight in front of you and keep your spine tall.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale as you hinge forward from your hips.
Hold the stretch comfortably, keep your back long, and breathe slowly.

exercises.name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana)
exercises.overview: A beginner-friendly backbend yoga pose where the hips are lifted off the floor forming a bridge shape, strengthening the posterior chain while opening the chest and stretching the hip flexors and spine.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens glutes and hamstrings; opens chest and hip flexors; relieves lower back pain; improves posture; reduces stress and anxiety; stimulates digestion
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, bend your knees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Press your feet down and slowly lift your hips and back off the ground, rolling shoulders underneath.
Hold for 10–15 seconds breathing steadily, then slowly lower back down and relax.

exercises.name: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)
exercises.overview: A powerful standing yoga pose where one leg lunges forward and arms reach overhead, building strength, stability, and focus while opening the chest and hips simultaneously.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens legs and core; opens hips and chest; improves balance and posture; boosts circulation; reduces stress; increases hip flexibility and range of motion
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, step one foot back 3–4 feet and angle it outward at 45 degrees, front foot pointing forward.
Bend your front knee to 90 degrees over your ankle, keeping your hips squared to the front.
Raise both arms overhead with palms facing each other, lift your chest, hold, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Moon Pose (Ardha Chandrasana)
exercises.overview: A graceful single-legged standing yoga pose where the body forms a half-moon shape, balancing on one leg while extending the other parallel to the floor and reaching both arms in opposite directions to build balance, strength, and flexibility.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens legs, core, and glutes; improves balance and stability; opens chest and hips; relieves back pain; reduces stress and anxiety; improves digestion and circulation
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, shift your weight onto one foot, and place your fingertips on the floor 8–12 inches in front of you.
Lift your opposite leg straight back parallel to the floor and extend your top arm upward, stacking both arms in a line.
Hold steady, breathe evenly for 15–30 seconds, then lower your leg and switch sides.

exercises.name: Plank Pose (Phalakasana)
exercises.overview: A foundational yoga pose where the body is held straight and firm like a plank, supported on hands and toes, deeply engaging the core, arms and shoulders while building full body strength and stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens core, arms, shoulders and wrists; improves posture and balance; tones abdominal muscles; relieves sciatica; builds full body endurance and stability
exercises.instructions:
Start on all fours, hands shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide, wrists directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core, tuck your toes, and step both legs back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Hold steady, keep hips level and do not let them sag or rise ,then gently lower your knees to exit.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold (Uttanasana)
exercises.overview: A fundamental standing yoga pose where you hinge forward at the hips and let the upper body fold down toward the floor, deeply stretching the entire back body while calming the mind and relieving tension.
exercises.benefits: Stretches hamstrings, calves and spine; relieves lower back tension; improves posture; stimulates digestion; reduces stress and anxiety; boosts circulation to the brain
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, and take a deep breath to lengthen your spine.
Exhale, hinge forward from your hips, and reach your hands toward the floor and bend knees if needed.
Let your head hang freely, hold for a few breaths, then slowly rise back up.

exercises.name: Low Lunge (Anjaneyasana)
exercises.overview: A foundational kneeling yoga pose where one leg lunges forward and the back knee rests on the mat, deeply stretching the hip flexors and opening the chest while building strength, balance and stability throughout the body.
exercises.benefits: Stretches hip flexors and groin; strengthens legs and core; opens chest and shoulders; improves balance and posture; stimulates digestion; reduces stress and back pain
exercises.instructions:
Step one foot forward between your hands, knee over ankle, and gently lower your back knee to the mat.
Inhale, lift your torso, and raise both arms overhead keeping shoulders relaxed and core engaged.
Hold for a few breaths, gently sink your hips forward, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: Chair Pose (Utkatasana)
exercises.overview: A powerful standing yoga pose where you sit on an imaginary chair with knees bent and arms raised overhead, deeply engaging the legs and core while opening the chest and shoulders to build strength, focus and stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens quadriceps, glutes and calves; tones core and lower back; improves posture and balance; stimulates digestion; reduces stress; enhances mental focus and concentration
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, and raise both arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Bend your knees and push your hips back and down as if sitting on an imaginary chair, keeping chest lifted.
Hold for a few breaths with knees behind toes, then press through your feet to rise back up.

exercises.name: Triangle Pose (Trikonasana)
exercises.overview: A foundational standing yoga pose where the body extends sideways forming a triangle shape, deeply stretching the legs, hips and spine while strengthening the core and improving balance and mental focus.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens legs, core and shoulders; stretches hamstrings, hips and spine; improves balance and posture; relieves back pain and sciatica; reduces stress and anxiety; stimulates digestion
exercises.instructions:
Stand with feet 3–4 feet apart, right foot turned out 90 degrees, and raise both arms parallel to the floor.
Hinge sideways from your hips, reaching your right hand down to your shin or floor and left arm straight up.
Hold for a few breaths keeping your torso long, then rise back up and switch sides.

exercises.name: Corpse Pose (Shavasana)
exercises.overview: A deeply restorative yoga pose practiced at the end of a session where you lie flat on your back in complete stillness, allowing the body and mind to fully absorb the benefits of the practice and enter a state of deep healing and relaxation.
exercises.benefits: Reduces stress and anxiety; lowers blood pressure; relieves muscle tension; improves sleep quality; enhances mental clarity and focus; promotes deep healing and cell repair
exercises.instructions:
Lie flat on your back, legs slightly apart, arms alongside your body with palms facing up.
Close your eyes, relax every muscle from head to toe, and breathe slowly and deeply through your nose.
Stay still for90 seconds, then gently wiggle fingers and toes, roll to one side, and slowly sit up.

exercises.name: Alternating V-Up
exercises.overview: A dynamic core exercise where you alternate lifting one leg at a time while crunching your torso up to reach the opposite arm toward the raised leg, forming a V-shape and deeply engaging the abs and obliques.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens rectus abdominis and obliques; improves balance and coordination; tones entire core; reduces lower back pain; enhances hip flexor strength and athletic performance
exercises.instructions:
Lie flat on your back, arms extended overhead, legs straight and feet 6 inches off the ground.
Lift one leg up and crunch your torso, reaching your opposite arm to touch that shin.
Lower back down keeping feet off the ground and repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Twist - Reverse (Ardha Matsyendrasana)
exercises.overview: A classic seated yoga twist where you rotate your torso in the opposite direction of the bent knee, deeply mobilizing the spine, massaging the abdominal organs and releasing tension built up across the back and hips.
exercises.benefits: Improves spinal mobility and posture; stretches outer hips and shoulders; relieves back pain; stimulates digestion; reduces stress and anxiety; increases energy and focus
exercises.instructions:
Sit tall, bend your right knee and place your foot outside your left thigh, left heel tucked near your right hip.
Place your right hand behind you, inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and twist left, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee.
Hold for a few breaths breathing steadily, then gently release and switch sides.

exercises.name: Butt Kicks
exercises.overview: A dynamic cardio exercise where you jog in place while rapidly kicking your heels up toward your glutes, activating the hamstrings, warming up the lower body and improving running mechanics and stride efficiency.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens hamstrings and glutes; improves cardiovascular fitness; increases hamstring flexibility; enhances running speed and coordination; burns calories; warms up lower body
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, core engaged, and arms bent at 90 degrees at your sides.
Jog in place, alternately kicking each heel up toward your glutes, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Pump arms in sync with the opposite leg, gradually build speed and maintain a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: Bottom Leg Lift (Right)
exercises.overview: A side-lying exercise where you lie on your right side and lift the bottom leg upward to target the inner thigh adductor muscles, improving hip stability and lower body strength.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens inner thighs and adductors; improves hip stability and pelvic control; tones lower body; enhances balance; prevents knee and hip injuries
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your right side with legs stacked, bend your top knee and place your top foot flat on the floor in front of you for support.
Exhale and slowly lift your bottom leg 6–12 inches off the floor, squeezing your inner thigh muscles.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Bottom Leg Lift (Left)
exercises.overview: A side-lying exercise where you lie on your left side and lift the bottom leg upward to target the inner thigh adductor muscles, improving hip stability and lower body strength.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens inner thighs and adductors; improves hip stability and pelvic control; tones lower body; enhances balance; prevents knee and hip injuries
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your left side with legs stacked, bend your top knee and place your top foot flat on the floor in front of you for support.
Exhale and slowly lift your bottom leg 6–12 inches off the floor, squeezing your inner thigh muscles.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Butterfly Pose (Baddha Konasana)
exercises.overview: A beginner-friendly seated yoga pose where the soles of the feet are brought together and knees fall out to the sides like butterfly wings, deeply opening the hips and inner thighs while calming the nervous system.
exercises.benefits: Stretches inner thighs and groin; opens hips and improves flexibility; strengthens pelvic floor; improves posture and spinal alignment; reduces stress and anxiety; stimulates digestion and pelvic circulation
exercises.instructions:
Sit tall, bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees fall out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles, draw your heels toward your pelvis, and lengthen your spine tall.
Breathe deeply and with each exhale allow your knees to gently drop lower — hold for 30–60 seconds.

exercises.name: Happy Baby Pose (Ananda Balasana)
exercises.overview: A gentle supine yoga pose where you lie on your back, hold the outer edges of your feet and pull your knees toward your armpits like a happy baby, deeply releasing the hips, inner thighs and lower back while calming the mind.
exercises.benefits: Opens hips and inner thighs; relieves lower back tension; stretches hamstrings and groin; improves spinal mobility; reduces stress and anxiety; stimulates digestion; promotes deep relaxation
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, bend both knees toward your chest and open them slightly wider than your torso.
Reach inside your knees and hold the outer edges of your feet, soles facing up toward the ceiling.
Press your feet into your hands and pull down gently, keeping your lower back flat on the floor.

exercises.name: Garland Pose (Malasana)
exercises.overview: A deep squatting yoga pose where the feet are flat on the floor and knees are wide apart, forming a deep hip opener that stretches the groin and inner thighs while strengthening the lower body and stimulating the digestive organs.
exercises.benefits: Opens hips and groin; improves ankle flexibility; strengthens legs and core; supports pelvic health; stimulates digestion; relieves lower back tension; improves posture and spinal alignment
exercises.instructions:
Stand with feet wider than hips and toes turned out, then bend your knees and lower into a deep squat with heels flat.
Bring palms together at your chest and press your elbows against the inner knees to open the hips wider.
Keep your spine tall and chest lifted, breathe steadily and hold for 30–60 seconds.

exercises.name: Diamond Push Up
exercises.overview: An advanced push-up variation where hands are placed close together forming a diamond shape under the chest, shifting the workload heavily onto the triceps while also engaging the chest, shoulders and core for a powerful upper body workout.
exercises.benefits: Builds tricep strength and definition; increases chest and shoulder activation; improves core stability; enhances pushing power; requires no equipment; boosts upper body endurance
exercises.instructions:
Get into a plank, bring hands together under your chest with thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond shape.
Keeping elbows tucked at 45 degrees, slowly lower your chest toward your hands until it almost touches the floor.
Push through your palms to fully extend your arms back to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Donkey Kicks (Right)
exercises.overview: A quadruped exercise where you kneel on all fours and kick your right leg up toward the ceiling with knee bent, isolating the glute muscles to build strength, improve hip stability and tone the entire posterior chain.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens and tones glutes; improves hip stability and pelvic control; activates core; corrects muscle imbalance; improves posture; low impact and joint-friendly
exercises.instructions:
Get on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, back flat and neck neutral.
Squeeze your glutes and kick one leg up with knee bent at 90 degrees until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower your knee back down without touching the floor and repeat all reps before switching sides.

exercises.name: Donkey Kicks (Left)
exercises.overview: A quadruped exercise where you kneel on all fours and kick your left leg up toward the ceiling with knee bent, isolating the glute muscles to build strength, improve hip stability and tone the entire posterior chain.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens and tones glutes; improves hip stability and pelvic control; activates core; corrects muscle imbalance; improves posture; low impact and joint-friendly
exercises.instructions:
Get on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, back flat and neck neutral.
Squeeze your glutes and kick one leg up with knee bent at 90 degrees until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower your knee back down without touching the floor and repeat all reps before switching sides.

exercises.name: Diagonal Plank
exercises.overview: An advanced plank variation where you hold a plank position and simultaneously extend the opposite arm and leg diagonally, challenging the core, improving balance and coordination, and building full body stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens core and spinal stabilizers; improves balance and coordination; activates glutes and shoulders; enhances posture; builds functional full body strength; reduces lower back pain
exercises.instructions:
Get into a high plank with hands under shoulders and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and slowly raise one arm straight forward and the opposite leg straight back, both parallel to the floor.
Hold for 2 seconds, lower back with control, then repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.overview: A supine core stability exercise where you lie on your back and slowly extend opposite arm and leg toward the floor while keeping the lower back pressed flat, deeply engaging the deep core muscles and improving coordination and spinal control.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens all four abdominal muscle groups; improves spinal stability and posture; enhances balance and coordination; reduces lower back pain; safe for all fitness levels and older adults; ideal for rehabilitation
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, raise arms straight up to the ceiling and lift legs with knees bent at 90 degrees, lower back pressed firmly into the floor.
Slowly lower your right arm behind your head and extend your left leg toward the floor at the same time, keeping your core tight.
Return to the start position and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press (Both Hands)
exercises.overview: A foundational seated upper body exercise where both dumbbells are pressed overhead simultaneously from shoulder height, isolating the deltoids and building shoulder strength, stability and size with reduced momentum compared to the standing variation.
exercises.benefits: Builds shoulder strength and size; improves shoulder stability; corrects muscle imbalances; enhances upper body pressing power; tones arms and shoulders; supports posture and spine alignment
exercises.instructions:
Sit upright on a bench, hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward and elbows at 90 degrees.
Exhale and press both dumbbells straight up until arms are fully extended — do not lock your elbows.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Side Lateral Raise
exercises.overview: An isolation shoulder exercise where dumbbells are raised out to the sides until arms are parallel to the floor, targeting the lateral deltoids to build shoulder width, definition and that classic V-shaped upper body.
exercises.benefits: Builds shoulder width and definition; improves shoulder stability; enhances athletic performance; corrects shoulder imbalances; improves posture; easy to perform with minimal equipment
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing in and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both arms out to the sides until parallel to the floor, leading with your elbows not your hands.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to your sides with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl (Left)
exercises.overview: A seated single-arm isolation exercise where the left elbow is braced against the inner thigh and the dumbbell is curled upward in a focused arc, maximizing bicep tension and eliminating momentum for superior muscle contraction and peak development.
exercises.benefits: Isolates and strengthens left bicep; improves bicep peak and definition; corrects left-right muscle imbalance; enhances mind-muscle connection; reduces momentum cheating; accessible for all fitness levels
exercises.instructions:
Sit on a bench, place your elbow against the inside of your thigh just above the knee, arm hanging straight down with palm facing forward.
Curl the dumbbell upward in a smooth arc toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm pressed firmly against your thigh.
Squeeze your bicep hard at the top, then slowly lower back to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl (Right)
exercises.overview: A seated single-arm isolation exercise where the right elbow is braced against the inner thigh and the dumbbell is curled upward in a focused arc, maximizing bicep tension and eliminating momentum for superior muscle contraction and peak development.
exercises.benefits: Isolates and strengthens right bicep; improves bicep peak and definition; corrects left-right muscle imbalance; enhances mind-muscle connection; reduces momentum cheating; accessible for all fitness levels
exercises.instructions:
Sit on a bench, place your elbow against the inside of your thigh just above the knee, arm hanging straight down with palm facing forward.
Curl the dumbbell upward in a smooth arc toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm pressed firmly against your thigh.
Squeeze your bicep hard at the top, then slowly lower back to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunges
exercises.overview: A lunge variation where one foot steps diagonally behind and across the other in a curtsy-like motion, uniquely targeting all three glute muscles — including the often-neglected gluteus medius — along with the inner thighs and quads for improved lower body strength and hip stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens glutes, quads and adductors; targets gluteus medius more than standard lunges; improves hip stability and balance; corrects lower body muscle imbalances; enhances coordination; burns calories
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, core engaged, hands on hips.
Step one foot diagonally behind and across the other leg, lowering hips until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Press through your front foot to rise back to start, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: Crunch Kicks
exercises.overview: A lying core exercise where you perform a crunch while simultaneously extending one leg straight out and then kicking it back in, targeting the lower abs and hip flexors while building core stability and endurance.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower abs and core; improves hip flexibility; activates glutes and quads; builds core endurance; requires no equipment; suitable as a warm-up or core finisher
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, hands lightly behind your head.
Crunch up lifting your shoulders off the ground while extending one leg straight out.
Kick the leg back toward your chest, lower shoulders to start, and alternate legs each rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.overview: An isolation exercise where you stand holding dumbbells at your sides and elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears, directly targeting the upper trapezius muscles to build neck and upper back strength, thickness and improved posture.
exercises.benefits: Builds upper trapezius strength and size; improves posture and spinal alignment; enhances shoulder stability; supports compound lifts like squats and deadlifts; corrects upper back imbalances; accessible and easy to learn
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing each other and arms straight.
Shrug both shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible and squeeze your traps hard at the top.
Pause for a second, then slowly lower your shoulders back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Kickbacks
exercises.overview: An isolation exercise performed in a bent-over position where the elbow is kept stationary while the forearm is extended backward, targeting all three heads of the triceps for arm definition and pushing strength.
exercises.benefits: Isolates and strengthens triceps; improves elbow stability; builds arm definition; low wrist stress; enhances pushing power; easy to program for all fitness levels
exercises.instructions:
Hinge forward, hold dumbbells and raise elbows to shoulder height with upper arms parallel to the floor.
Extend both forearms straight back until arms are fully locked, squeezing triceps hard at the top.
Slowly bend elbows back to 90 degrees and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Punches
exercises.overview: A boxing-inspired cardio exercise where you alternately punch forward with light dumbbells, building shoulder and arm endurance while elevating the heart rate and improving coordination and upper body speed.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens shoulders and triceps; improves cardiovascular endurance; boosts coordination and speed; burns calories; builds functional upper body strength; improves punching power
exercises.instructions:
Stand with knees slightly bent, hold light dumbbells at chest height with palms facing each other.
Punch one arm forward, rotating your wrist palm-down at full extension — do not lock the elbow.
Return to start and immediately punch with the other arm, alternating in a steady controlled rhythm.

exercises.name: Froggy Glute Lifts
exercises.overview: A prone floor exercise where you lie face down, bring your feet together in a frog position with knees wide, and lift both knees off the ground by squeezing the glutes, deeply targeting all three glute heads and the underbutt area with no equipment needed.
exercises.benefits: Targets all three glute heads; tones and lifts the underbutt; strengthens hamstrings and lower back; improves hip stability; low impact and joint-friendly; no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Lie face down, bend both knees and bring feet together with knees spread wide out to the sides in a frog position.
Squeeze your glutes and lift both knees off the floor simultaneously, pressing heels together.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower your knees back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.overview: A supine core exercise where both legs are raised slightly off the floor and alternately kicked up and down in a rapid fluttering motion, targeting the lower abs and hip flexors while building core endurance and stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower abs and core; improves hip flexor endurance; enhances core stability and posture; burns calories; low impact; builds coordination and body awareness
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back, hands tucked under your glutes, lower back pressed firmly into the floor.
Lift both legs 6–12 inches off the ground and engage your core tightly before moving.
Alternate kicking one leg slightly higher while lowering the other in a quick controlled flutter, keeping your back flat.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Raise
exercises.overview: A standing calf raise performed with one or both hands lightly touching a wall for balance, where you rise up onto the balls of your feet to strengthen the calf muscles, improve ankle stability and build lower leg definition safely and effectively.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens gastrocnemius and soleus; improves ankle stability and joint health; enhances balance; reduces risk of ankle injury; improves posture; easy to perform anywhere with no equipment
exercises.instructions:
Stand facing a wall, fingertips lightly touching it for balance, feet hip-width apart and back straight.
Press through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as possible, squeezing your calves at the top.
Hold for 1–2 seconds, then slowly lower your heels back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.overview: A static lower body exercise where you slide your back down a wall until thighs are parallel to the floor and hold the seated position, building quad strength and muscular endurance through isometric contraction with no equipment required.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens quadriceps, glutes and hamstrings; builds muscular endurance; improves core stability and posture; rehabilitates knee injuries; burns calories; suitable for all fitness levels
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your back flat against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart and about 2 feet away from the wall.
Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and knees are at 90 degrees over your ankles.
Hold the position, breathe steadily and keep your back firmly pressed into the wall for as long as possible.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
exercises.overview: An isolation shoulder exercise where dumbbells are raised straight in front of the body to shoulder height with palms facing down, targeting the front deltoids to build shoulder definition, improve posture and strengthen pushing movements.
exercises.benefits: Builds anterior deltoid size and definition; improves posture and shoulder symmetry; enhances overhead pressing strength; strengthens front shoulder for daily lifting activities; easy to learn for all fitness levels
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold dumbbells in front of your thighs with palms facing down and a slight bend in elbows.
Raise both dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your torso upright, do not swing.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Standing Side Bend
exercises.overview: A standing bodyweight exercise where you raise one arm overhead and bend your torso sideways to stretch and strengthen the obliques and lateral core muscles, improving spinal flexibility, waist definition and side-to-side stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens and tones obliques; improves spinal lateral flexibility; relieves back and hip muscle tension; enhances posture and core stability; easy to perform anywhere with no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart, and raise one arm straight overhead close to your ear.
Slowly bend your torso to the opposite side as far as comfortable, feeling the stretch along your raised arm side.
Return to upright, complete all reps, then switch sides and repeat.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Ups
exercises.overview: A beginner-friendly push-up variation performed standing against a wall, reducing body weight resistance to build chest, shoulder and tricep strength safely — ideal for beginners, older adults and those recovering from injuries.
exercises.benefits: Builds upper body strength with low joint stress; improves chest and shoulder definition; enhances core stability; easy progression toward floor push-ups; suitable for rehabilitation; no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Stand facing a wall, place hands flat on the wall slightly wider than shoulder-width at chest height.
Keep body straight, bend your elbows and lean your chest toward the wall until your nose nearly touches it.
Push through your palms to straighten arms back to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl (Overhand Grip)
exercises.overview: A bicep curl variation performed with an overhand (pronated) grip where palms face downward, shifting the primary workload from the biceps to the brachioradialis and brachialis muscles to build forearm thickness, grip strength and balanced arm development.
exercises.benefits: Builds brachioradialis and forearm strength; improves grip endurance; corrects arm muscle imbalances; enhances wrist and elbow joint stability; develops well-rounded arm definition
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold dumbbells with an overhand grip (palms facing down), arms extended at your sides.
Keeping upper arms still and elbows tucked, curl both dumbbells upward toward your shoulders with wrists straight.
Squeeze at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: V Hold
exercises.overview: An isometric core exercise where you balance on your sitting bones with both legs and torso raised off the floor forming a V shape, deeply engaging the entire abdominal wall and hip flexors while building core strength, stability and balance.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens entire core including upper and lower abs; improves balance and body control; builds spinal stability; enhances hip flexor strength; improves posture; no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Sit on the floor, lean back slightly and place hands lightly behind your thighs for support.
Lift both feet off the floor, straighten your legs and raise your torso to form a V shape, balancing on your sitting bones.
Hold steady, breathe evenly, keep your back straight and core tight, then slowly lower back down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.overview: A bicep curl variation performed with a neutral grip where palms face inward, shifting emphasis onto the brachialis and brachioradialis to build arm thickness and grip strength.
exercises.benefits: Builds arm thickness and definition; strengthens brachialis and brachioradialis; improves grip strength; corrects arm muscle imbalances; enhances pulling performance
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold dumbbells with palms facing inward, arms fully extended at your sides.
Keep upper arms still, curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders without rotating your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then slowly lower back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Superman Hold
exercises.overview: A prone isometric exercise where you lie face down and simultaneously lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor to strengthen the entire posterior chain and improve spinal stability.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens lower and upper back; improves posture and spinal stability; activates glutes and hamstrings; reduces lower back pain risk; no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Lie face down, arms extended overhead, legs straight and forehead resting on the floor.
Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor, reaching fingertips and toes as far apart as possible.
Hold for 3 to 5 seconds breathing steadily, then slowly lower everything back down and repeat.

exercises.name: Camel Pose (Ustrasana)
exercises.overview: A kneeling backbend yoga pose where you arch the spine backward and reach both hands to your heels, deeply opening the chest and hip flexors while strengthening the back and improving spinal mobility.
exercises.benefits: Opens chest and hip flexors; improves spinal flexibility and posture; stimulates digestion; relieves mild back pain; reduces stress; stimulates thyroid gland
exercises.instructions:
Kneel on your mat, knees hip-width apart, hands on hips and inhale to lengthen your spine tall.
Exhale, arch your back and slide your palms toward your heels, keeping your neck neutral.
Hold for a few breaths, then place hands back on hips and slowly return upright.

exercises.name: Easy Pose (Sukhasana)
exercises.overview: A foundational seated cross-legged yoga pose used for meditation and breathing exercises, gently opening the hips and inner thighs while promoting spinal alignment, calmness and mental focus.
exercises.benefits: Opens hips and inner thighs; improves posture and spinal alignment; reduces stress and anxiety; promotes mental clarity; strengthens core; accessible for all ages
exercises.instructions:
Sit on your mat, cross your shins and draw each foot beneath the opposite knee, knees falling outward.
Sit tall on your sit bones, lengthen your spine and rest your hands on your knees.
Relax your shoulders, soften your gaze and breathe deeply and steadily.

exercises.name: Hero Pose (Virasana)
exercises.overview: A kneeling yoga pose where you sit between your heels with thighs internally rotated, deeply stretching the quadriceps, ankles and feet while promoting spinal alignment and aiding digestion.
exercises.benefits: Stretches quadriceps, ankles and feet; improves digestion and circulation in legs; relieves tired legs; reduces lower back pain; improves posture; relieves menstrual discomfort
exercises.instructions:
Kneel on your mat, shins flat, knees together and feet spread just wider than your hips.
Slowly lower your buttocks to the floor between your feet — use a block if needed.
Sit tall, lengthen your spine, rest hands on thighs and breathe steadily.

exercises.name: Staff Pose (Dandasana)
exercises.overview: A foundational seated yoga pose where you sit with legs extended straight and spine held tall like a staff, building core and back strength while improving posture and serving as the base for all seated yoga poses.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens core and back muscles; improves posture and spinal alignment; stretches hamstrings; increases body awareness; improves respiratory function; reduces stress
exercises.instructions:
Sit on your mat with both legs extended straight, feet together and toes pointing up.
Place hands flat beside your hips, sit firmly on your sit bones and lengthen your spine upward.
Lift your chest, pull shoulders back and down, and breathe steadily for 8 to 10 breaths.

exercises.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Row
exercises.overview: A compound pulling exercise where you hinge forward at the hips and row both dumbbells toward your waist, building a thick strong back by targeting the lats, traps and rhomboids while improving posture and pulling power.
exercises.benefits: Builds upper and mid-back thickness; improves posture; corrects muscle imbalances; enhances pulling strength; engages core stabilizers; balances out pressing exercises
exercises.instructions:
Hinge forward at your hips, torso nearly parallel to the floor, arms hanging straight down.
Drive your elbows back and pull both dumbbells toward your waist, squeezing shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back down with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Jumping Rope
exercises.overview: A classic full-body cardio exercise where a rope is swung overhead and jumped over repeatedly, strengthening the calves while elevating heart rate, improving coordination and burning a high number of calories in a short time.
exercises.benefits: Improves cardiovascular fitness; strengthens calves and legs; burns calories rapidly; enhances coordination and balance; improves bone density; boosts agility and footwork
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall, hold one handle in each hand and swing the rope overhead in a smooth arc.
Jump lightly off the balls of your feet — just 1 to 2 inches off the ground — elbows close to your sides.
Land softly with knees slightly bent and maintain a steady rhythm throughout.

exercises.name: Leg In and Out
exercises.overview: A seated core exercise where you balance on your sit bones and alternate between pulling your knees toward your chest and extending your legs out, deeply engaging the abs and hip flexors while building core endurance.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens upper and lower abs; improves core stability and endurance; enhances hip flexor strength; improves balance and body control; no equipment needed
exercises.instructions:
Sit on your mat, hands behind your hips, lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor.
Pull your knees toward your chest — this is the in position.
Extend your legs straight out while leaning slightly back — this is the out position — repeat without touching the floor.

exercises.name: Side Plank (Left)
exercises.overview: An isometric core exercise performed on the left side where you support your body on your left forearm and feet, forming a straight diagonal line to deeply engage the obliques and lateral core stabilizers.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens obliques and lateral core; improves spinal stability and posture; reduces lower back pain; enhances balance and coordination; builds hip abductor strength
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your left side, left forearm flat on the mat with elbow directly under your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Hold steady, breathe evenly and keep hips lifted — do not let them sag.

exercises.name: Side Plank (Right)
exercises.overview: An isometric core exercise performed on the right side where you support your body on your right forearm and feet, forming a straight diagonal line to deeply engage the obliques and lateral core stabilizers.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens obliques and lateral core; improves spinal stability and posture; reduces lower back pain; enhances balance and coordination; builds hip abductor strength
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your right side, right forearm flat on the mat with elbow directly under your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Hold steady, breathe evenly and keep hips lifted — do not let them sag.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise (Left)
exercises.overview: A side-lying exercise where you lie on your right side and raise your top left leg upward to target the hip abductors, strengthening the outer glutes and improving hip stability and pelvic control.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens hip abductors and outer glutes; improves hip and pelvic stability; reduces knee and hip injury risk; corrects muscle imbalances; improves balance; safe and low impact
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your right side, legs stacked straight, head supported and left hand on the floor for balance.
Keeping your left leg straight, slowly raise it upward to 30 to 45 degrees, squeezing your outer glute.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down without resting on the bottom leg and repeat.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise (Right)
exercises.overview: A side-lying exercise where you lie on your left side and raise your top right leg upward to target the hip abductors, strengthening the outer glutes and improving hip stability and pelvic control.
exercises.benefits: Strengthens hip abductors and outer glutes; improves hip and pelvic stability; reduces knee and hip injury risk; corrects muscle imbalances; improves balance; safe and low impact
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your left side, legs stacked straight, head supported and right hand on the floor for balance.
Keeping your right leg straight, slowly raise it upward to 30 to 45 degrees, squeezing your outer glute.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down without resting on the bottom leg and repeat.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Crunch
exercises.overview: A crunch variation performed on a stability ball that provides a greater range of motion than floor crunches, increasing abdominal muscle activation by up to 38% while also improving core stability, balance and coordination.
exercises.benefits: Increases abdominal muscle activation; improves core stability and balance; greater range of motion than floor crunches; reduces lower back stress; engages deep stabilizer muscles; tones and strengthens the entire core
exercises.instructions:
Sit on the stability ball and walk your feet forward until your lower back rests on the ball, knees bent and feet flat.
Engage your core and curl your upper body upward until your shoulders lift off the ball — do not pull on your neck.
Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down over the ball and repeat.
